beats.got: Picking a tool because we own the platform is a bad reason. I have seen that in IT proposals.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: The plan is not done when the technical half is polished and nobody owns it. Every failed programme I have seen looked like that. There is still no cost line anywhere.

beats.got: A licence or a copied agent file gives a generic answer, and then people stop using it. That is what a licence is worth.

take_homes: Count real use separately from access. Ask for both numbers before I believe any rollout saving.
A rollout plan with unnamed owners is not a plan. Check for names first.
Before buying or rolling out a tool, ask what would have to be true for the person to drop what they use today.

monday.move: Ask my controller who actually uses the licences we already pay for. Ask how they do the month-end variance commentary today and what would make them switch. Ask for the usage figure, not the seat count.
monday.stop_condition: If the usage data takes more than a day to produce, I drop it and treat that as the answer.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, so I can only ask about current use and cannot try anything new.

misconception.why: The point that access and absorption get reported as one number made me doubt that a licence is the whole thing. I still don't see a cost or payback figure, so I haven't fully changed.

one_line: No numbers and no cost anywhere, but it told me why our rollouts stall: we count licences and nobody counts who actually uses them.
